feature.title: cpp: Introduce ParameterHandler for asynchronous parameter operations
feature.author: gasmith
feature.scope_decision: C++ SDK plus C ABI glue over the fixed Rust core (the PR's own boundary). The Rust ParameterHandler trait and responders already exist at the base commit; the agent designs the FFI surface (opaque responders, handler struct, option fields), regenerates the cbindgen header, and writes the C++ wrapper. Remote access is built (compile-verified) but only the WebSocket path is exercised at runtime.

oracle.reference: Rust SDK WebSocketServer (rust/foxglove at the base commit, unchanged by the PR) running the same scripted ParameterHandler; transcripts of one scripted ws-protocol client (Python websockets 15.0.1) must be identical for the C++ server, the C server and the Rust server. Plus: the PR's 5 Catch2 cases and the 71 upstream Catch2 cases (exact count 76, one process per case via ctest), the gold param-server example compiled against the submitted API, cargo test -p foxglove_c, cbindgen header-in-sync check, and compile-only deprecation probes.
oracle.python_sdk_note: The Python SDK at this commit has no ParameterHandler (only the legacy listener callbacks), so it cannot serve as a reference for the new API; the Rust SDK is the sole cross-implementation reference. A Python wheel was therefore not built into the verifier image.

contamination.notes: Merged 2026-05-23, 3.5 months before authoring (below the 2026-06 preference in the pack README). Interface names are the upstream ones (not shifted). PR body, Linear ticket FLE-533, and the C++ docs page for ParameterHandler are public.

horizon.proxy: 17 files, +1294/-125 non-test (about 900 hand-written lines across Rust FFI and C++), 3 subsystems (C ABI crate, C++ WebSocket server wrapper, C++ remote-access wrapper) plus cbindgen configuration and header regeneration; hidden tests exercise ownership transfer across the FFI boundary, precedence, capability inference, echo/no-echo, drop-to-error-status, thread hand-off and exception containment.

derivability.assertion: hidden: 'ParameterHandler requires both onGet and onSet' - only onGet or only onSet -> WebSocketServer::create returns FoxgloveError::ValueError; neither -> create succeeds
derivability.instruction_ref: C++ API / Contract, first bullet: 'if exactly one of onGet / onSet is set, return FoxgloveError::ValueError ... If neither is set, no handler is registered.'

derivability.assertion: hidden: 'get and set echo to requester' - onGet receives request_id 'get-1' and names [foo, bar] in order; respond() sends parameterValues with that id; onSet receives request_id and views; respond echoes with id
derivability.instruction_ref: C++ API / Contract bullets 2-3 (request id, names in request order, ParameterView) and C API contract bullet 3 (get response to requester, set echo when request carried an id)

derivability.assertion: hidden: 'set without request_id does not echo' - no parameterValues arrives after a set without id
derivability.instruction_ref: C API contract bullet 3: 'a set response is echoed to the requester only when the request carried a request_id'

derivability.assertion: hidden: 'dropping responder sends error status' - status level 2 with message containing 'failed to send a response'
derivability.instruction_ref: C API contract bullet 3 and C++ contract bullet 3: destroying an un-responded responder performs the drop, 'generic error status to the requester (level error, message stating that the parameter handler failed to send a response)'

derivability.assertion: hidden: 'publish after respond broadcasts to subscribers' - server.publishParameterValues called inside onSet delivers an id-less parameterValues filtered to the subscription; setter still gets its echo
derivability.instruction_ref: C++ contract bullet 4: 'Calling WebSocketServer::publishParameterValues ... from inside a handler callback is allowed and is the way to broadcast applied updates'

derivability.assertion: hidden tests include <foxglove/parameter_handler.hpp> and use foxglove::ParameterHandler, GetParametersResponder, SetParametersResponder with the exact std::function signatures and `std::move(responder).respond({})`
derivability.instruction_ref: C++ API code block and 'Add the public header cpp/foxglove/include/foxglove/parameter_handler.hpp'

derivability.assertion: build_example: gold param-server example compiles: `options.parameter_handler = handler;` (copy of a ParameterHandler), responders stored in a struct and moved into a worker queue, completed later
derivability.instruction_ref: 'ParameterHandler is a plain aggregate ... (copyable and movable)'; 'Responders can be moved into another thread and completed there'; evaluation item 2

derivability.assertion: parity/handler: serverInfo advertises 'parameters' although the driver sets no capability
derivability.instruction_ref: C API contract bullet 4 and C++ contract bullet 1: registering a handler 'implies the Parameters capability'

derivability.assertion: parity/handler: unknown names are absent; unset_param is filtered out of get responses; 'all parameters' when names is empty
derivability.instruction_ref: 'empty means all parameters'; 'Parameters whose value is unset are dropped by the core before serialization' (the driver script defines which names exist)

derivability.assertion: parity/handler: a get whose handler throws std::runtime_error yields the generic error status and the connection remains usable
derivability.instruction_ref: C++ contract bullet 5: exception must not propagate; un-consumed responder destroyed -> error status; 'The connection stays usable.'

derivability.assertion: parity/handler: a get completed from a detached thread 100 ms later is answered normally
derivability.instruction_ref: 'Responders can be moved into another thread and completed there'; C API: '*_respond ... later from any thread'

derivability.assertion: parity/precedence: with legacy callbacks returning a sentinel and a handler registered, responses come from the handler
derivability.instruction_ref: C API contract bullet 4 / C++ bullet 1: handler 'takes precedence over the legacy callbacks, which are then never invoked'

derivability.assertion: parity/legacy: with only legacy callbacks and the Parameters capability, get/set echo and automatic subscriber publication behave as before
derivability.instruction_ref: C API contract last bullet: 'legacy callbacks keep their exact current behavior (including the automatic publication ...)'; C++ bullet 6: 'keep working when no handler is registered'

derivability.assertion: parity_c: C driver compiles against the generated header using foxglove_parameter_handler{context,get,set}, foxglove_server_options.parameter_handler, foxglove_*_responder_respond/drop, and produces the reference transcript; foxglove_gateway_options.parameter_handler exists (compile-only)
derivability.instruction_ref: C API code block and 'appended as the last member of both foxglove_server_options and foxglove_gateway_options'

derivability.assertion: api_validation: C++ create() rejects half-set handlers with ValueError and accepts none/both
header_in_sync: submitted foxglove-c.h equals cbindgen output of submitted c/src + cbindgen config
derivability.instruction_ref: Scope and rules bullet 4: 'The committed header ... must be exactly what cbindgen generates'
